text.text:
Yann LeCun just launched AMI, and named it "friend" (ami in French 🇫🇷). 

LeCun left Meta in November, raised $1.03B in the largest seed round ever by a European startup, at a $3.5B valuation announced March 10, 2026. The company is called Advanced Machine Intelligence. 

His core argument: "The real revolution is not AI replacing humans, but AI helping humans think better, plan better, and understand the real world." And: LLMs "don't really deal with the real world", they can pass the bar exam but can't navigate physical reality, which is why we don't have domestic robots or level-5 self-driving cars.

In a world of agents and automation, the most human thing you can build is something that helps people think better.

text.text:
Yesterday marks the end of my one-year internship at Pints AI, and it feels strangely bittersweet.

When I first stepped in, I thought this year would mostly be about learning new technologies and gaining industry experience. It was, but it was also so much more than that. It challenged the way I think, pushed me to question existing paradigms, and taught me that growth often comes from moments when you’re unsure but willing to try anyway.

There were days where things worked beautifully, and days where nothing seemed to go according to the gameplan. But those moments ended up being the most valuable. They taught me how to adapt, how to think deeper about problems, and how to keep moving forward even when the path wasn’t obvious.

What made this journey truly special, though, were the people. To my mentors, Gabriel L. and Soksedtha Ly, thank you for your patience, guidance, and for trusting me with real problems that helped me grow beyond what I expected. And to all the amazing coworkers I had the chance to work alongside: thank you for the conversations, the collaboration, and the little moments that made the workplace feel welcoming every day.

I’m leaving this chapter not just with new skills, but with new perspectives, stronger curiosity, and a deeper appreciation for the people who make meaningful work possible. Grateful for everything this year has taught me. 

On to the next chapter.
